value: A direct comparison between the TDP-43-positive and tau-positive groups found no regions involved to a greater degree in the tau-positive group, and the scattered regions of greater temporal lobe loss in the TDP-43-positive group did not survive correction for multiple comparisons. Thus, there was no signature pattern of atrophy distinguishing tau from TDP-43 pathology.

spans.text: A direct comparison between the TDP-43-positive and tau-positive groups failed to find any regions that were involved to a greater degree in the tau-positive group even when the data was uncorrected for multiple comparisons. The TDP-43-positive group had a few scattered regions of greater loss in the temporal lobes compared to the tau-positive group (uncorrected, p < 0.001), although these regions did not survive a correction for multiple comparisons using the FWE correction (p < 0.05), or the more lenient FDR correction (p < 0.01).

spans.text: Patients with bvFTD who had a CDR score of 0.5 showed gray matter loss predominantly in the medial, orbital and dorsolateral aspects of the frontal lobes, as well as the anterior insular, anterior cingulate gyrus, and anterior hippocampus compared to controls (fig. 3). More severe involvement of these regions was identified at CDR 1 with additional widespread involvement of the temporal lobes as well as the posterior cingulate gyrus and parietal lobe (fig. 3). Once again, a more severe pattern of loss was observed in patients who had a CDR of 2 or 3 with more severe involvement of all structures and additional bilateral involvement of the striatum (fig. 3).

description.value: This study used volumetric MRI and voxel-based morphometry to assess gray matter loss associated with autopsy-confirmed tau-positive and TDP-43-positive frontotemporal lobar degeneration and with clinical disease severity.
An observational study of autopsy-confirmed FTLD subjects and age- and gender-matched healthy controls, with prospective clinical follow-up and MRI acquisition.

model_settings.value: Voxel-based morphometry using an optimized SPM2 method with customized templates and prior probability maps; images were normalized, segmented, modulated, and smoothed with an 8-mm FWHM kernel. Age and gender were included as nuisance variables; time from onset to scan was additionally included for the bvFTD pathology comparison.
